title: Online convex optimization in general norms: full subgradients and Bregman geometry.
summary: Losses are convex, with full subgradients bounded in the specified dual norm, and actions lie in a public convex set. A public strongly convex regularizer supplies the Bregman geometry and initial radius. The target is static regret; geometric operations and loss feedback are charged separately.

model.instance: The compact convex set $X\subset\mathbb R^d$, norm $\|\cdot\|$, and dual norm $\|\cdot\|_*$ are public. Each loss $f_t$ is convex, and the returned valid subgradient satisfies $g_t\in\partial f_t(x_t)$ and $\|g_t\|_*\le G_*$. The regularizer $\psi$ is differentiable on a neighborhood of $X$ and $1$-strongly convex in the specified norm. The public initial point $x_{\mathrm{init}}\in X$ satisfies $$D_\psi(u,v)=\psi(u)-\psi(v)-\langle\nabla\psi(v),u-v\rangle,\qquad \sup_{u\in X}D_\psi(u,x_{\mathrm{init}})\le R_\psi^2.$$. The environment may fix losses in advance or select them from the history consistently with current subgradient feedback, without anticipating current private randomness.

bounds.derivation: Choose step size $\eta=\sqrt2R_\psi/(G_*\sqrt T)$. The Bregman three-point inequality gives $\sum_t\langle g_t,x_t-u\rangle\le R_\psi^2/\eta+\eta G_*^2T/2$; convexity yields the regret bound. The proof holds pathwise, so random or adversarial selection of a valid full subgradient does not change it.
